long_biography.plain_text:
Four vehicles ordered in 1955 began Abdul Latif Jameel's relationship with Toyota and established the automotive base Mohammed Jameel later inherited. With an MIT degree in civil and environmental engineering, he joined the family operation and eventually served as its chairman and chief executive.

Under Jameel's stewardship, the business carried its distribution expertise into new countries and built substantial operations in finance, real estate, renewable energy, water infrastructure, consumer products, media and healthcare. The result is a diversified family group active across six continents, with Jameel still serving as chairman. He created Community Jameel in 2003 to organise the family's philanthropic work and remains its founder and chairman. That institution is separate from the commercial group. His sons Fady and Hassan now hold vice-chair roles in family businesses and philanthropies, distinguishing the third generation from Mohammed's second-generation stewardship.
